newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thai baht, stocks firm on IMF relief package.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thai baht, stocks firm on IMF relief package.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed slightly on Wednesday on growing relief offered by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan pledge but the topside was limited on jitters over widening currency woes in Asia.
"The IMF (rescue package) has turned the baht slightly bullish. Corporate demand for dollars has also slowed as they seem to think the baht might firm a bit more yet," said one trader at a Thai bank.
The rescue loan pledge worth $16 billion made on Monday by the IMF and Asian nations also provided some comfort in buying battered Thai stocks, but profit-taking capped any sharp gains.

Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Wednesday that Thailand will start tapping loans from the IMF-initiated loan package when its foreign reserves fall below a level sufficient for financing four months of imports.
The closely-watched composite SET index ended up by a scant 0.48 points or 0.08 percent at 632.73 with the upside limited at 639.88. The SET-50 index also rose 0.07 points to 47.93.

The baht meanwhile firmed to 31.43/55 to the dollar late in the onshore market from 31.60/31.70 in early morning trade. But it was still weaker than 31.30/31.35 late on Monday. Tuesday was a public holiday to observe Queen Sirikit's birthday.
The baht's upside was limited by jitters over Asian currency turmoil, which took a fresh twist on Wednesday with the Indonesian rupiah diving to a historic low against the dollar.
The Indonesian central bank later provided some support by raising domestic interest rates and also stepping into the currency market to defend the currency.
The Singapore dollar also remained under pressure, but recouped some of its losses on talk of possible central bank intervention to defend the currency, dealers said.
Traders who returned from the one-day public holiday here initially jumped on a bandwagon to snatch up the U.S. dollar as a safe haven, but such dollar buying later petered out.
In the offshore market, the baht was quoted at 31.40/50 late on Wednesday compared with 31.20/31.30.
On the stock market, the regional currency turmoil erased most gains on the back of the IMF-led package. Declines led advances 134 to 90 with 72 issues closing unchanged.
"There was selling pressure in some bank and finance shares in the afternoon. Some investors took profit on early gains," said a broker at Ekkapat Finance and Securities.
Thai Farmers Bank headed the active list, losing one baht to 111, Bangkok Bank rose five to 168.

Lingering political jitters also weighed on the Thai financial markets, as Bangkok's plan to raise the value added tax (VAT) to 10 percent from seven percent from August 16 intensified criticism against Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.
Thanong said on Wednesday he did not expect inflation to surge to double digits after Thailand adopted the tough austerity measures in the bailout package.
The finance minister, asked if Thailand's decision to raise VAT would stoke inflation, said: "We should not be over concerned. Inflation will unlikely reach double digits."
